asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Hand over the {material}.
Go up and make what is there stretch.
Take the supplier's name and move on.

g2.text:
The course goes on before the light goes, and the roof is a roof by dark.
{stranger} pays over the odds and will not be argued down: {payment}, counted into {leader}'s hand on the tailgate, and the first rain that night lands on finished work.

hh.text:
An afternoon of passing, holding, and not looking down, and what is there stretches further than the arithmetic said it could.
The gap that is left is small enough to tarpaulin with dignity. Payment in {payment}, and a standing welcome under the roof the party {helped close|closed|got a course onto}.

hf.text:
A batten gives, and for one long second the yard is a good deal closer than planned.
Caught, mostly, by the trestle and partly by {stranger}, at the cost of a bruise shaped like carpentry. The tarpaulin goes on in silence.

e5.text:
The supplier's name goes in {the diary|the book|the back of the diary} under things that can be fixed by somebody with a full pack and a free morning.
Behind, on the roof, the hammering starts again anyway, slower, {weather}.

qe_bet.title: {The Fair|The Stall That Does The Arithmetic|Small Stake, Big Pot}

n0.text:
A fair at {place}: {many} stalls, one band, and one stall taking money on {a strength machine|a ring toss that is not as easy as it looks|a card the whole crowd is sure it can follow}.
{stranger} runs it with the face of somebody who has done the arithmetic and sleeps well on it. The stake is small. The pot is not.

asides.hedonistic: {member} has already lost twice and is having a wonderful time.
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Put the stake down and play.
Read the trick before spending a coin.
Just enjoy the fair.

wb.text:
The pot pays out to a stall-holder's round of applause, which is how a professional buries a bad quarter of an hour.
The crowd carries {leader} to {bar} on the strength of it and the story is already growing on the way.

lb.text:
The arithmetic was theirs all along, the way it always was.
The stake is gone, the crowd is kind about it, and the {drink} afterwards tastes of being one more person the stall has put through the same {short education|brief education|short lesson}.

rb.text:
The trick is {in the thumb|in the felt|in the count}, and once seen it cannot be unseen.
One play, placed properly, and a quiet exit at the pace of somebody who knows exactly how long a stall-holder takes to {work out what just happened|catch up|do that arithmetic}.

lb2.text:
After {forty minutes|an hour|half an evening} of watching, the only firm discovery is that the stall has been watching back, with professional interest, since minute five.
No coin has changed hands. Both sides understand it is a draw, and there is a strange courtesy in {the nod exchanged at parting|the nod at the end of it|how the nod is given}.

v2.text: The band is {loud|too loud|loud and not good}, {food} is exactly what it should be and no better, and for one whole evening the party's line of work does not come up once.

qe_pilgrim.title: {The Pilgrim|Short Of The Shrine|A Vow With A Deadline}

n0.text:
{stranger} is sitting against {sign} at {place}, sweating, {weather}, a good way short of where a vow says they must stand by dark.
Something's wrong in the chest and they will not name it, on the reasoning, common among the devout and the frightened, that naming a thing invites it in.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Give what medicine the pack holds.
Treat it in the field, bare-handed.
Carry them the rest of the way.

gm.text:
The herbs do what herbs do, slowly, and the colour comes back in the wrong order but it comes back.
The pilgrim pays in the only coin the order deals in: a prayer that works, taught word-perfect on the walk that is left, with strict instructions about {when never to use it|the one hour it must never be used|who it must never be used on}.

wt.text:
Breathing settles under {leader}'s hands the old way: posture, pressure, and a voice kept deliberately boring.
The last stretch is walked slow, together, and at the shrine the pilgrim stands there before dark, and does not look back, and does not need to.

wf.text:
Whatever is wrong in that chest is above field repair and everybody kneeling on the verge knows it.
What can be done is done: shade, water, and company, which is not nothing. The vow is missed. The pilgrim says the deadline mattered less than the walking, and almost sounds {convinced|as if they mean it|like somebody who believes it}.

ct.text:
{distance}, most of it uphill, all of it in the open, {weather}, in relays.
The shrine appears around the last bend with ten minutes of the light left, and the pilgrim arrives carried, which their order, consulted afterwards, rules is arriving all the same.

cf.text:
Four kilometres of it, and then the party's legs file a formal objection on a wet slope.
Everybody sits on the wet slope for a while, wrecked together, and the pilgrim laughs for the first time all day, which is worth something even if nothing else was {reached|arrived at|got to}.

qe_lockup.title: {Lot 41|The Lockup Nobody Claimed|Keys That Do Not Fit}

n0.text:
A lockup at {place}, sold at auction {timeAgo} to a bidder who never came for it.
{stranger} has a ring of keys that do not fit, a paper that says the contents are theirs if the door is open by dark, and an offer: the party opens it, the party gets a share of whatever is shelved inside.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.impulsive: {member} has tried three keys already, on the grounds that somebody had to.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Pick it.
Force the door.
Read the auction paper properly first.

pl.text:
The lock is old and proud and gives up its dignity one pin at a time.
Inside: shelves, packed by somebody methodical, and the party's share of it fills the packs to the straps. {stranger} keeps the paper and the story, and considers it {a bargain|a good trade|well bought}.

fl.text:
The door loses{, eventually| in the end| on the fourth go}, but takes its toll on the way down: half of what was shelved behind it does not survive the argument.
The half that does is still a good afternoon's work by {weight|weight alone|any measure}.

pf.text:
The door wins the first two rounds and part of the third, and by dark it is still shut and the paper is so much kindling.
{stranger} is decent about it, which stings worse than the knuckles.

ip.text:
The paper is genuine, and better than genuine: down in the schedule, in the small type, is an inventory the seller never read.
{leader} names a fairer split before a single key turns, with the inventory as the argument, and it is agreed to at speed. The door, tried once more with feeling, opens after all on {the plainest key on the ring|a key nobody had bet on|the one key that looked wrong for it}.

e6.text:
The small type defeats {the light|the eyes|everybody in turn} and the light is going.
Some doors keep their afternoons. The keys go back in a pocket, the paper back in its envelope, and the lockup keeps its shapes, plural, for {another owner|the next owner|somebody else entirely}.

q_leyline.title: {The Broken Line|Where The Magic Stopped|Dry Ground}

n0.text:
Nothing casts at {place}. Not badly: at all. {member} tries the smallest cantrip anybody knows and {ground} takes it like a stone taking rain.
Somebody broke the line here, and did it on purpose, from the look of the burn pattern. {asker} is camped a hundred metres off the dead spot with {instrument} and a face that says this is week three.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Splice the line with {qty} {material}.
Read the burn and work out who broke it.
Whatever wanted this ground dry is still here. Find it.

sp.text:
The splice is ugly work with the party's own stock and it holds on the second attempt.
The line comes back the way a tap comes back: air first, then everything at once. Every hair on the away team stands up, and for one second {leader} can feel where every other line on this {rock|world|whole rock} runs.

rd.text:
The break was cut from underneath and cut clean, which takes a contract and a specialist, not an accident.
{asker} looks at the diagram for a long time and then names a price for the party never having drawn it: {payment}, and the diagram goes in the fire.

rf.text:
The burn reads as an accident right up until the party is a day gone and {member} sits up in the dark having worked out what was wrong with the third measurement.
By then it is somebody else's {dead ground|problem|dead ground entirely}.

oil.text:
Down under {remnant}, in a cut nobody made with tools, something is sitting in its own weight and waiting for the line to come back.
Without the leyline it cannot regenerate. That is the entire reason the line was cut, and whoever cut it never came back to {finish the job|finish it|do the second half}.

amb.text: {It finds the party first|It is already moving when they turn|It comes up out of the cut first}, which on dry ground means finding them without {a single spell|one spell|anything at all} between them and it.

q_grimoire.title: {The Book That Is Eating Itself|Bad CamelCase|Burn It Or Do Not}

n0.text:
A book at {place}, out of the weather under {remnant}, open, with something wrong on the left-hand page.
One formula in it has the words apart. It has been copying itself into its neighbours for a while now, and the neighbours have started agreeing with it. {sound}, and the pages are warm.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Burn it. That is the procedure.
Cut out the clean pages first.
Copy the infected formula down properly before it goes.

burn.text:
It goes up fast and it argues on the way, which books do not usually do.
What is left is a clean patch of {ground} and the flat certainty of having done the correct thing, which is worth {less on the walk home than it should be|surprisingly little on the walk home|almost nothing by the time the ship is in sight}.

cut.text:
{few} pages come out clean with the knife, taken from the outside in, ahead of the spread.
The rest burns. What is saved is worth carrying: workings from before whoever wrote this got careless, in a hand that never once {separated a word|let a word come apart|got one wrong}.

cop.text:
Writing it out correctly is the hardest {hour|two hours} anybody has spent sitting down. The formula does not want to be joined up and says so in the wrist.
Joined up, it is a real thing, and a considerable one. The book goes on the fire immediately afterwards and nobody {argues|says a word|objects}.

spread.text:
It gets into the party's own notes before anybody notices the handwriting changing.
Everything written down in the last {few} days has to be burned in a heap on {ground}, and it takes a piece out of everyone to do it.

q_kessler.title: {Above The Cage|The Armoured Rocket|What Came Down Instead}

n0.text:
Something came down at {place} that was built to be destroyed on the way up: layered plate, sacrificial, a hull that is nine tenths armour and one tenth room.
One of the armoured launches, then, and this one did not dock. {instrument} says there is still power in it. {wrongness}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Cut in.
Power the beacon up with {qty} {material} and let somebody else come for it.
Strip the plate and go.

inn.text:
Inside: {three couches, two of them used|four couches, three of them used|three couches and two sets of boots}, and a log kept by hand right up until it was not.
They got through the debris. They got through it and the docking never happened and they came down here instead, and somebody wrote all of it down for whoever {opened the door|got here|came}.

cx.text:
Sacrificial plate is sacrificial in every direction. The layer that gives gives all at once, and takes {the back of a hand|a length of forearm|two fingers' worth of glove} with it on the way past.
The door stays shut. Whatever is behind it {stays behind it|stays there|is left there}.

bea.text:
The beacon takes the {material} and lights, and starts saying the same four words to an orbit nobody can currently cross.
Somebody will hear it eventually. The party's registry is in the header, and that is a name in a file at a space centre, which is a thing that pays out later and pays out {well|very well|better than the job did}.

str.text:
The plate comes off in {sheets|slabs|long curved pieces} and it is good plate: rated for the grinder, which means rated for anything the party is likely to walk into.
The couches stay where they are. Nobody says anything about the two that are used, and nobody {has to|needs to|does}.

n0.text:
{vessel} sits at {place} with the ramp down and {cargo} half unloaded onto {ground}.
Nobody is aboard. The manifest is on a clip by the ramp, filled in properly all the way to the third page, and then not at all.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.loyal: {member} {positions themselves between {leader} and the door|nods firmly: "Right behind you, boss."|keeps a watchful eye on {leader}'s blind spot|stands ready to back up whatever call is made}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Finish the unload and leave the manifest signed.
Take a share and go.
Wait for whoever is coming back.

fin.text:
It is {four|five|three} hours of honest work and the ramp is clear by the end of it, everything squared, the clip signed with the party's own registry.
The crew, when they come back, come back at a run, and the arithmetic of what they were expecting to find against what is actually standing there does something to their faces. The Society pays its debts {the same day|before dark|inside the week}.

hurt.text:
A drum that had to stay upright does not, and the corner of it finds {a shin|an ankle|the outside of a knee} on the way over.
The rest gets unloaded slower and worse. It is still unloaded, and the clip {still gets signed|gets signed|is signed at the end of it}.

take.text:
What comes away fits in the packs and is worth having, and the manifest never had a fourth page to disagree with.
Somewhere {ahead|down the route|at the far end of this} there is a hauler who is going to stand at the bottom of a ramp doing arithmetic. The Society keeps a very long memory and {a very dense network|a network to match|no gaps anywhere in its network}.

wait.text:
Two hours on the ramp with {sound} for company, and then they come over the rise carrying the fourth page and a story about why.
Nobody is robbed, everybody eats, and the party leaves with a name to use at any fire on this route and the number of an old handset that {always answers|answers at any hour|has never once not answered}.

q_verden.title: {The Planted Limb|What Grows Back|Two Of Them Now}

n0.text:
There is a garden at {place}, laid out in rows on ground that grows nothing, and a blue-skinned figure working it who greets the party in flawless MarkovSpeak and keeps working.
One of the rows is an arm. It is planted at the wrist, it is not dead, and it is further along than it was {last week|a week ago|when the rows were last counted}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Give {qty} {material} for the beds.
Work the rows for a day.
Ask what they threw into a star, and why.

gv.text:
The beds take it and the gardener's hands go straight to work with it, no thanks offered, because thanks are for strangers.
What comes back at the end of the row is a cutting of something that should not root in {ground} and does, and instructions for it that take an hour and are given twice {to be sure|over|to make certain}.

wk.text:
A day in the rows: heavy, repetitive, done properly, in company that talks the whole time and says something worth keeping about {one hour in six|twice an afternoon|more often than that}.
By dark the party has been fed twice and given a name that works in any Verden household on {any world|any world at all|whichever world they are on}.

wf.text:
The rows win. Nobody warned the party that a Verden day is measured against a Verden back.
The gardener finds this funnier than anybody has found anything in weeks and packs the party off with food and a genuinely sympathetic pat that nearly puts {leader} in {the bed|the row|the soil}.

ask.text:
The answer takes the walk to the end of the row and back and is not a lament.
They put the whole of it into the sun on purpose, all of it, and there is nothing in the telling that regrets it, and by the end {leader} is no longer certain the party's own pockets represent the winning side of {the argument|it|that particular argument}.

q_magamui.title: {One At A Time|The Quiet One In The Camp|Whose Idea Was It}

n0.text:
A survey camp at {place}, {few} of them, and every one of them can tell you exactly whose idea it was to dig here except the one whose idea it was.
They are all agreed it was a good idea. They are agreed in the same words. {wrongness}, and one of them has not blinked since the party walked in.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Work out which one is being ridden.
Get the camp away from the dig, all of them, now.
Not the party's dig, not the party's camp.

id.text:
It's not the quiet one. The quiet one is {exhausted|running on nothing|three days past sleeping}, and has been carrying the whole camp's shifts because everybody else keeps forgetting they agreed to take them.
It is the one who has been most reasonable all afternoon. The Guild has standing orders about this and they are one line long, and it needs doing before the thing gets time to {move house|change tenant|find somebody else}.

ev.text:
It takes the whole of {leader}'s voice and every hour of daylight, and the camp comes off the dig in one piece and stays off it.
Up on the ridge, with distance under them, {few} of them start crying and one of them starts remembering things about the last month that had not previously happened to anybody.

wrong.text:
The party picks the wrong one, and the camp closes round the mistake the way a hand closes.
It is a bad {half hour|twenty minutes|hour} and only some of it is remembered afterwards, in the wrong order, by {different people|three different people|everybody differently}.

left.text:
Behind, the camp goes back to agreeing with itself, in the same words, on the same ground.
{member} writes the coordinates down and underlines them, which is what you do when you {cannot do anything|can do nothing else|have nothing else to give}.

q_pigeon.title: {Ninety Kilometres An Hour|The Bird With The Stick|Post}

n0.text:
There is a loft at {place}, built out of {remnant} and considerable stubbornness, and {asker} keeping {many} birds in it against {hazard}.
Nothing electronic gets in or out of here. The birds do, at ninety with a tailwind, with a stick tied to the leg, and one of them has not come back.

asides.loyal: {member} {positions themselves between {leader} and the door|nods firmly: "Right behind you, boss."|keeps a watchful eye on {leader}'s blind spot|stands ready to back up whatever call is made}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go and find the bird.
Give {qty} {material} for the loft and carry the post yourselves.
Ask what is on the sticks.

fnd.text:
It is down under {remnant} with a wing that will mend and a stick still on the leg, and it puts up a fight about being picked up, which is a good sign in a bird.
What is on the stick is somebody's whole year. The loft pays in the only currency that means anything out here, which is being owed something by {a keeper of birds|the keeper of a loft|somebody who keeps birds}.

nof.text:
Two days of {ground} and {hazard} and nothing with feathers on it anywhere.
The keeper takes the news the way keepers do, which is by going to feed the others.

car.text:
The loft gets its {material}, and the party gets a satchel of sticks and a route, and does the round on foot because a hull would never make the last leg.
Every stop on it is somebody who has not heard from anybody in a season. Nobody lets the party leave without feeding them {first|first, properly|before anything else}.

asked.text:
Births, mostly. Prices. Two deaths that people needed to know about in an order that mattered.
One stick is not read out. It goes in a box with {lots} others, and the keeper says the box is for after, and does not say {after what|what after means|any more than that}.

q_father.title: {What Fell|The Piece Of Him|Nothing Grows Around It}

n0.text:
Something came down at {place} that is not debris, and {ground} for {few} metres around it has stopped doing anything at all: no dust settling, no {sound}, nothing rotting.
{instrument} will not read it. Reading it is not the sort of thing it is for. {asker} is kneeling at the edge of the circle, and has been for some time.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Touch it.
Get it covered and get word out.
Leave it where it fell.

touch.text:
It is cold and it is not stone and something goes up the arm and keeps going.
When it lets go, the world is arranged slightly differently and {leader} has something they did not {Walk in|Step through the entrance|Cross the threshold|Head inside} with, and no training anywhere accounts for it, which is {exactly the point of it|the whole point of it|the point}.

cov.text:
The {material} goes over it and the circle goes under a cairn, and the position is written down twice in two different hands.
The kneeling one thanks the party in a language that ran out of speakers a while ago, and pays in the way of people with nothing: {everything they have|all of it|what little there is}.

lv.text:
It stays where it fell with somebody kneeling at the edge of it, and the party walks out through ground that starts behaving normally again about {forty|thirty|fifty} paces on.
It is a relief. Nobody expected it to be {a relief|that|one}.

q_prospect.title: {The Claim|Markers In The Ground|Two Names On One Patch}

n0.text:
Two sets of claim markers at {place}, driven into the same {ground}, {few} paces apart, both of them legal on paper somewhere.
{asker} has one set. The other set's owner is due back at any hour, and there is exactly one seam under all of it. {sound}, which does not help anybody's nerves.

asides.calm: {member} suggests that a seam under two claims is a bigger seam than either of them costed for.
asides.aggressive: {member} has already worked out which set of markers comes out easier.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Broker it before the other one gets back.
Survey the seam properly and let the ground decide.
Pull the other set of markers.

bro.text:
A split, in writing, witnessed by {three|four} people who do not like each other, which is the strongest kind of witnessing there is.
The other one arrives to a signed page instead of an argument and takes twenty minutes to stop looking for the catch. The party's cut is written in as brokerage, which nobody {objects to|argues with|queries}.

sur.text:
The seam runs {the other way entirely|nothing like where either paper says|at right angles to both of them}. Both claims clip the shoulder of it and neither of them sits on it.
The real body is out under open ground nobody has papered at all, which the party knows first and by {some distance|a clear margin|a day at the least}.

brf.text:
The other one gets back mid-sentence and has been rehearsing {on the walk|the whole way up|since the last ridge}.
It goes the way these go, at speed, in the wrong order, on ground neither of them will {get to keep|keep|hold by the end of it}.

pull.text:
The markers come out {easily|without much argument|one-handed}. That is the trouble with markers.
Someone's going to walk back onto this patch and find their year gone, and the party is paid in ore for having made it happen {quickly and quietly|quickly|without a word said}.

n0.text:
There is a handset at {place}, an old indestructible brick of a thing, wired into {remnant} by somebody who knew what they were doing.
It is tuned. That is the point of it being here. {asker} has been keeping the site since before the party landed and will not touch it, and is very clear that the not touching is a decision and not a fear.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Call.
Retune it with {qty} {material} and hand it back to the keeper.
Cut the line.

ans.text:
Something picks up on the fourth ring and does not say hello.
What it says instead takes eleven seconds and is answering a question nobody in the party has asked out loud, and afterwards {leader} sits down on {ground} for a while.

wrongno.text:
Something picks up. It's not what the tuning was for. It stays on the line after the handset goes down and it is still there, faintly, under {sound}, for the whole walk out.
{member} does not sleep properly for a while after.

ret.text:
The {material} does it. The tuning comes back true and the keeper takes the handset in both hands and looks at it, and then at the party, and asks them to go outside for a minute.
Whatever gets said in there takes longer than a minute. Afterwards the keeper is different in the face and pays {over the odds|far over the odds|more than was asked}.

cut2.text:
The wire parts and the warmth goes out of the casing in about {a second and a half|two seconds|the time it takes to put it down}.
The keeper says thank you, and means it, and is crying, and means that {too|as well|just as much}.

q_lavabath.title: {Harmless Now|The Pool That Drains You|In Up To The Knee}

n0.text:
There is a working at {place} where {ground} opens onto a pool that ought to be lethal and is not, since the Squishing took the heat out of the argument.
Doesn't burn. It drains. {asker} has {few} people going in to the knee in shifts to pull something out of the bottom, and they are coming out empty and grey.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Take a shift.
Rig a way to do it without anybody going in.
Ask what is down there first.

gotit.text:
Two minutes in the pool costs about what an hour of hard casting costs, and the second minute costs more than the first.
What comes up on the third shift is worth every unit of it, and {asker} says so, and pays like somebody who has been waiting {a long time|weeks|the whole season} to pay somebody.

drain.text:
It takes more than it was supposed to, all at once, near the end of the shift.
{leader} comes out on somebody else's shoulder, empty to the floor of the tank, and it takes until the next day to be worth {talking to|much|anything at all}.

rig.text:
The {material} makes a grab and a line and a frame to hang the whole thing off, and it takes three attempts and works on the fourth.
Nobody goes in the pool again. That is the part of it the shift crew care about, and they are the ones who decide {what the party is paid|the rate|what it was worth}.

what.text:
{Somebody's brother|Somebody's daughter|Somebody's mate off the same shift}, is what is down there, from before anybody knew the pool did not burn.
The shifts are not mining. They have been going in to the knee in turns for {a fortnight|three weeks|eleven days} to bring somebody home, and did not think the party would help if they said so first.

choices.text: Then take a shift.
Rig the grab instead.

home.text:
It takes {the rest of the day|until dark|another six hours} and most of what everybody has, and it is done, and he comes up.
The camp does what camps do, which is to feed everyone at once and put the party in the middle of it and not let them pay for {anything ever again|a single thing|anything, ever}.

q_scrap.title: {A Scrap Of Creation|The Door In The Air|Test Ground}

n0.text:
There is a seam in the air over {place} about the size of a door, and behind it the light is the wrong colour and {ground} keeps going into somewhere that is not this rock.
It is one of the old test spaces. Something practised here, a long time ago, and did not clear up. {tone}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.impulsive: {member} has an arm through to the elbow, waving.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go through.
Peg it open with {qty} {material} and map the edge.
Mark it and walk away from it.

thr.text:
On the far side: a room the size of {a country|a weather system|somewhere that has a name} with one idea in it, worked out over and over on every surface until whoever it was got it right.
The last version of it is still there, finished, sitting on nothing, and it is not guarded because it never occurred to anybody that the room would be {found|found at all|walked into}.

lost.text:
The far side does not keep the same layout twice, and the door is not where the door was.
It takes {many} hours to get back out and everybody arrives on {ground} lighter than they went in, in ways that take inventory to establish.

peg.text:
The {material} holds the seam at the width it was found at, which is the whole trick: a scrap that is not measured is a scrap that closes.
The measurements are worth money to four separate parties and the party sells them once, to the one that will {publish|publish it|put it in print}.

mk.text:
A cairn, a bearing, {a page in the book|two lines in the log|a sketch nobody will believe}, and the light going on being the wrong colour behind them all the way to the horizon.
Some doors are for {telling somebody about|reporting|leaving to people better equipped}.

n0.text:
There are {few} people at {place} going about a working day with nothing behind the eyes at all.
They eat. They walk the same route. One of them is still doing a job that stopped mattering some time ago, in order, correctly, with nobody in there to do it. {wrongness}.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Find what took them.
Feed them and keep the routes clear.
Put them down.

found.text:
The residue is on {ground} in a ring, and it is not the sort of thing that goes off by itself, and there is a serial on the fragment.
That serial is a matter of very considerable interest to people who will pay for it and to people who will kill for it, and the party gets to choose which conversation to {have|have first|be in}.

nofound.text:
Whatever it was cleaned up after itself {thoroughly|to a standard|the way a professional does}, and the only evidence left walks around eating breakfast at the correct hour.
The party writes down what they saw. Writing it down is {what there is|all there is|the whole of what can be done}.

feed.text:
The stores go into the hoppers along the route and the route gets swept and the doors get propped where the doors were sticking.
They will go on until {the bodies stop|the last of them wears out|something else stops them}. Zero argument in which this was the useful thing to do, and everybody does it {anyway|anyway, all day|regardless}.

down.text:
It is quick, and quiet, and correct by every standard anybody has written down.
Nobody talks on the way back to the pad. {member} is sick behind a rock at the halfway mark and nobody mentions it {then or afterwards|then|at any point afterwards}.

q_road.title: {The Turn-Off|Road Where No Road Is|The Encompassing}

n0.text:
There is a road at {place}. Not a track: a road, made, cambered, with a white line down it, running out of {ground} at both ends into nothing.
{asker} is parked on the hard shoulder of it with the engine running and has been for a while, working up to something.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Get the engine calibrated with {qty} {material} and take the turn-off.
Walk it to the end.
Note the bearing and stay off it.

turn.text:
Calibrated right, the road ahead folds up {like a map being put away|the way a concertina goes|into itself}, and the turn-off is somewhere else entirely by the time the wheels reach it.
Wherever that was, the party was there for about four minutes and came back with things that are not sold anywhere {on this rock|in this system|anybody can name}.

walk.text:
It takes {all day|until the light goes|the better part of a day} and the road ends the way it began, cleanly, mid-camber, with the white line stopping at a right angle.
At the end of it there is a shrine of sorts, made by drivers, and everything on it was left by somebody who got somewhere. The party leaves something and takes nothing, and the walk back is shorter than the walk out by a margin nobody {wants to discuss|is willing to name|does the arithmetic on}.

loop.text:
Somewhere past the fourth hour the road starts arriving at itself. The same white line, the same {remnant} on the same side.
It takes {member} spotting their own bootprint going the other way to break it, and everybody comes off the surface onto honest {ground} feeling several hours poorer than the clock says.

off.text:
The bearing goes in the book and the road goes on lying there being a road.
{asker} is still parked on the shoulder when the party is a kilometre out, still working up to {it|whatever it is|the turn}.

qe_bubble.title: {The Edge Of It|Eighty Or Nothing|Tuesday Again}

n0.text:
{hour}, on the road out of {place}, the air ahead goes wrong in the way air does about {few} metres from the edge of one of them.
The map marks it. The map has not been redrawn since {timeAgo}, and the edge has moved. {stranger} is standing just on the safe side of the line with a bicycle and a face that says today is not the first time.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go in and bring whoever is in there out.
Re-mark the edge properly, all the way round.
Take the long way and say nothing to anybody.

outt.text:
Inside it is the same Tuesday it has been for a while and everybody in it knows, which is the part nobody prepares you for.
Getting out means going outward over eighty, and {vehicle} is not built for it, and it is done anyway with three people in the back holding on to each other and one of them {counting|counting out loud|watching the needle}.

stuck.text:
The run at the edge comes up short, and short means the whole thing again from the top, on the same Tuesday, with everybody's confidence a good deal thinner.
They get out on the {fourth|third|fifth} go. Some of the fourth go is not remembered, and the party comes out with a day of their own {missing|gone|unaccounted for}.

mark.text:
Posts and paint the whole way round, at the real edge, which takes until dark and a good deal more {material} than anybody estimated.
Everything that comes down that road for the next twenty years will slow for those posts. Nobody will ever know the party did it. The Society hears about it within a week.

away.text:
The long way is {an hour and a half|two hours} of bad surface and it is {an hour and a half|time|a detour} nobody complains about.
Behind, the map goes on saying what it has said since {timeAgo}, and the edge goes on being where it actually is.

qe_note.title: {The Security Strip|Notes With The Thread Picked Out|Small Denominations}

n0.text:
In a back room off {street} there is a table, a lamp, and {stranger} taking the security thread out of euro notes with a needle, one note at a time, into a saucer.
There is a lot in the saucer. The notes go back into circulation afterwards and nobody has ever noticed, because nobody has ever had a reason to look.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Buy the saucer.
Work out what it is for.
This is a currency offence and a considerably worse one underneath.

buy.text:
It changes hands into a tin and the tin goes into the pack wrapped in {cloth|a shirt|two layers of the same cloth}, because the pigment does not care for light.
What it is worth is not really a price. A round of it will kill somebody standing in a loop, and there is enough here for a round or two, and now that is the party's {problem to carry|problem|to carry}.

for.text:
Not counterfeiting. Coating.
There is a workbench under the table with {few} rounds on it, half done, and a list of names, and every name on the list is somebody who has been sitting inside a bubble being untouchable for years while people on the outside {had opinions about it|argued about it|wrote letters}.

forf.text:
The story holds all evening: {a hobby, a pigment, a private eccentricity|an old habit, a pigment, nothing in it|a collection, a pigment, a way to pass an evening}, and the saucer is just a saucer.
It is a good story and it is told by somebody who has had a long time to practise it, and the party leaves with nothing but a slight itch about the {third|second|fourth} answer.

rep.text:
It goes on paper and the paper goes in at the desk with {paper} attached, and the room is cleared within a day.
The party never learns which of the two possible reasons it was cleared for, which is its own {kind of answer|sort of answer|answer}.

qe_naguka.title: {Corpse Paint At The Crossroads|The One With The Wrong Face|Kin}

n0.text:
There is a Naguka sitting at the crossroads outside {place} with the paint half off, holding a broken instrument and no idea which direction is which.
The horde went that way {timeAgo}. This one did not, and cannot explain why in more than about {six|five|seven} words at a time, and keeps saying one of them.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.aggressive: {member} has counted the crossroads' sightlines and does not like any of them.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Feed it and take it as far as the next town.
Fix the instrument with {qty} {material}.
Hand it in at the barracks.

take2.text:
It eats like something that has not, and walks in the middle of the group without being asked to, and by the second hour is telling a story with about {eleven|nine|a dozen} words in it and using all of them twice.
At the town it is taken in by somebody who has done this before. The collective knows, within the day, that the party did not leave one of theirs {at a crossroads|in a ditch|standing at a crossroads}.

fix.text:
The {material} does it, roughly, and the first note out of it stops the conversation dead.
What it plays at the crossroads is not for the party and is not for anybody. Halfway through, {member} realises they are hearing something the horde is also hearing, {distance}, and gets very quiet.

hand.text:
The barracks take it and sign for it and are correct throughout, and the sergeant does not meet {anybody's eye|the party's eye|anybody's eye at all} while doing the signing.
The collective unconscious does not have a subtle way of registering an opinion, and it {registers one|registers this one|makes it known}.

qe_ttd.title: {Tinfoil|The Idea Going Round|Everybody Had It At Once}

n0.text:
Half of {place} is wearing hats and the other half is laughing at them, and the half wearing hats have a point.
There is a thought going round: the same {rumour}, arriving in the same words, in people who have not spoken to each other. {stranger} keeps a list of who has had it and the list is the wrong shape for gossip.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Dam it. Foil for everybody, {qty} {material} worth.
Find patient zero on the list.
Sit with it and see what it wants.

dam.text:
It looks ridiculous and it works, which is the whole history of the countermeasure in one sentence.
Inside two days the list stops growing. Nobody in {place} will ever be able to say whether it would have stopped anyway, and everybody {keeps the hat|keeps wearing the hat|hangs on to the hat}.

zero.text:
The list sorted by hour comes to a point, and the point is a man who has not left his house in {timeAgo} and did not think the thought either.
He received it. There is a difference and he is the only person in {place} who understands it, and he has been waiting for somebody to {come and ask|ask|turn up and ask}.

want.text:
Sat with properly, it is not a message. It is a shape, and the shape is trying to be held by enough people at once to become a thing.
{leader} does not let it, which is harder than it sounds and takes until the small hours, and the shape goes {looking elsewhere|somewhere else|off to be held by somebody else}.

caught.text:
Everybody in the party has it by the evening, in the same words, arriving at the same time.
It takes {few} days and a great deal of foil to get it back out, and for a while afterwards nobody trusts an idea they {had on their own|arrived at alone|came up with}.

qe_wellhead.title: {The Wellhead|Where The Line Comes Up|Oil And Blood}

n0.text:
There is a capped wellhead in the field beyond {place} with {sign} rusted off it, and everything green for {few} metres around it is growing the wrong way round.
The line comes up here. {stranger} has been paid by somebody to sit and watch it and has never been told what for, and has worked most of it out anyway.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Reseal it properly with {qty} {material}.
Open it.
Read the ground and find where the line actually runs.

seal.text:
The cap goes back on right this time, gasketed, with the {material} doing the work the original contractor was paid for and did not do.
The grass round it will take a season to remember which way up it goes. The cheques keep coming to the watcher, who is now watching a wellhead that is actually sealed, and says so, and pays {a share|a share of it|the party a share}.

open.text: What comes up is not {oil|oil at all|what the cap was for}, or is oil {in the way that a person is meat|the way a body is chemistry|only in the sense that it came out of the ground}.

line.text:
Doesn't run where the survey says. It runs under {place} itself, under the school and the market and the road, which is why everything in that town has always felt like it is about to happen.
What that map is worth depends entirely on who is shown it, and the party is holding the only {copy|copy there is|copy anybody has}.

linef.text:
The ground says four different things in four different places and none of them agree, which is what leylines do to anybody without the training.
{leader} comes away with a headache that lasts into the next day and a very clear sense of having been {read back|read in return|looked at by the ground}.

qe_grimoire.title: {The Shelf It Was Left On|Bad Spelling|Do Not Leave It Beside Anything}

n0.text:
A house clearance at {place}, and {stranger} standing in the doorway not going back in, holding the door with a boot.
On the shelf inside there is a book with a formula in it written with the words apart, and it has been on that shelf beside other books for {timeAgo}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Burn the shelf, the lot of it.
Sort the clean ones out of it.
Take the whole shelf to somebody who wants it.

burn2.text:
The whole shelf goes into the yard and goes up, and it takes longer than paper should and makes a noise about it.
{stranger} watches the entire burn from the gate and does not go back into the house until the ash is cold, and then pays the party in cash out of {a tin|a biscuit tin|the tin on the mantelpiece}.

sort.text:
Working from the far end inward, ahead of the spread, {few} volumes come off clean and one of them is not a grimoire at all: it is somebody's working notebook, and it is better than the grimoire ever was.
The rest goes on the fire and it is {a considerable fire|a fire the whole street comes out for|a bigger fire than the shelf accounts for}.

sp2.text:
It has been on that shelf {a long time|years|longer than anybody said} and it has been busy.
The formula is in the party's own pack before anybody checks, and everything written down in there has to come out and go on the fire, including {the map|the map, which hurts|two months of the map}.

sell.text:
There is always somebody who wants a shelf like that and never any difficulty finding them, which is the thing about people who want shelves like that.
The money is {good|better than good|more than the job was worth}. The buyer is delighted. Nobody involved has done anything that will look {well written down later|well in writing afterwards|good in anybody's account of it}.

n0.text:
{stranger} at {bar} in {place} has an old handset on the table, the indestructible kind, and it has rung twice this evening with no network anywhere near it.
Nobody has answered it. That is a house rule now, arrived at democratically, and the second ring emptied the far corner of the room.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Answer it.
Buy it off them.
Get it retuned properly, {qty} {material} of parts.

ansr.text:
It is somebody's grandmother, and she died in {timeAgo}, and she is not confused about that at all and would like the party to pass something on.
What she passes on takes ninety seconds, is entirely practical, and settles an argument in a family in {place} that has been running since before {anybody in the room was born|the war|any of them were born}.

bad.text:
Something answers that is enjoying being answered.
It asks {leader} a question by name, waits, and hangs up first, which is the part that {stays with everybody|nobody gets over|is still there in the morning}.

buy2.text:
The whole {bar} watches the money change hands and the whole {bar} is visibly relieved, and somebody stands the party a round on the strength of it.
It is a talisman as much as a phone: near it, a loop sits still and a fracture stays shut, and it rings when it wants to.

tune.text:
Retuned it stops ringing at random and starts ringing on purpose, which is either better or worse depending on the week.
{bar} keeps it on a hook behind the taps and treats it like a fire extinguisher, and the party drinks there free for as long as {the place stands|the doors are open|there is a bar there}.

qe_flood.title: {Sandbags|The Water Is Coming Up Through The Floor|By Morning}

n0.text:
The water is coming up through the floors on {street} in {place}, not down from the rain but up, and it has been rising since first light.
There are {many} houses on that row and about a third as many people to do anything about it. {stranger} is filling bags off the pile with the wrong shovel and will not stop long enough to be given a better one.

asides.nurturing: {member} has taken one end of a bag before anybody agrees anything.
asides.calm: {member} sends the first four people they can find to the top of the row instead of the bottom, and is right.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Bags, all night.
Give {qty} {material} to plug it at the source.
Get the people out and let the houses go.

held.text:
The row holds. It holds at about {four|half three|five} in the morning, and the last bag goes on at a point where nobody has anything left, and then it holds.
In the light everybody sits down in the mud at the same time. Somebody's mother goes down the row with tea and does not accept {any refusals|a single refusal|no for an answer}.

lost2.text:
It goes at the low end at about three and takes {few} houses with it, and the rest of the night is carrying furniture upstairs in the dark.
Nobody blames anybody. Everybody looks like they might, for a while, which is {worse|the harder part|worse than being blamed}.

src.text:
It's not the river. It is a culvert somebody built over {timeAgo} and nobody has looked at since, and the {material} plugs the mouth of it in an hour and a half by lamplight.
The water stops rising while people are still filling bags, and it takes the row {twenty minutes|the best part of an hour|a while} to believe it.

evac.text:
Everybody out, {up the hill|onto the high road|to the church, which is the high ground}, with what they can carry and the animals loose behind them.
The row goes. Nobody drowns, which was the actual question all along, and there is a difference between those two facts that takes people {a few weeks|the winter|months} to feel.

n0.text:
There is a borehole in the ground near {place}, capped, and the cap has been redone {few} times by different hands over the years, each one heavier than the last.
{stranger} is minding it out of a hut with a flask and no particular authority, and is not facing outward.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Reweld it, {qty} {material} of rod.
Listen at it.
Take the watch for a night so somebody can sleep.

weld.text:
The fifth cap goes on over the fourth and it is {the best of them|better than the four under it|the first one done by somebody who wanted it to hold}, done properly, with the rod the party carried in.
The minder watches every pass of it and afterwards sits down for the first time in the conversation. Whatever is down there is a good deal further away than it was {this morning|at breakfast|when the party walked up}.

lis.text:
There is a sound at the cap and it is not {water|rock} and it is not settling. It is a long way down and it is regular, and it is getting to the top of the shaft slightly faster than it did on the previous measurement.
Somebody at a desk somewhere has that measurement in a file and has decided not to be the person who says it {out loud|first|at all}.

lisf.text:
Whatever is down there hears the listening.
It stops, all at once, for as long as the ear is on the plate, and starts again the moment it comes off, and {leader} does not sleep well for {a while|some nights|the rest of the season}.

watch.text:
A night in a hut with a flask and a chair facing the wrong way, listening to nothing for {eleven|nine|ten} hours.
The minder sleeps for the first time in a fortnight, in a bed, in a house, and comes back at dawn with breakfast for everybody and an old story that is not in {any archive|any file anywhere|the record}.

qe_hauler.title: {Under Eighty All The Way|The Load That Cannot Stop|Relief Driver}

n0.text:
A hauler is stopped on the hard shoulder outside {place} with the hazards going and {stranger} asleep against the wheel in the way of somebody who has fought it and lost.
The load has to be somewhere by first light and the route has {few} marked bubbles on it, and neither of those facts is going to negotiate.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Drive it. Relief for the last leg.
Sit in the cab and keep them talking to the depot.
Not the party's load and not the party's licence.

drv.text:
It is {distance}, holding a heavy thing under eighty past marked ground with somebody asleep in the bunk behind, and it is the most concentrated three hours anybody has spent this month.
The depot signs for it on the hour, exactly. The Society pays relief rates, and relief rates are not what anybody expects.

drf.text:
The speedo gets away on a downgrade for about {four|three|five} seconds and four seconds is plenty.
Correcting it costs the load a pallet and the party's nerves the rest of the day, and the depot is late, and the sign-off happens anyway with everybody being {very polite about it|extremely polite|careful about it}.

talk.text:
{Four|Five|Three} hours in a cab with a flask, keeping somebody awake by making them describe every depot between here and the coast.
By the end there is a name for every stop on that route, which of them will let you sleep in the yard, and which of them owes the Society a favour that can be {signed over|called in|passed on}.

no.text:
The hazards are still going in the mirror {a long way down the road|most of the way to the next junction|for longer than anybody watches}.
Whether they made it is a thing the party never finds out, which is the ordinary condition of most of the good one might have done.

qe_saint.title: {The Reliquary|{saint} Is Missing A Hand|Feast Day Is Thursday}

n0.text:
The reliquary at {place} is open and light and the wrong weight, and the feast is on Thursday.
{stranger} has told nobody yet and is standing in the sacristy working out whether telling nobody is a sin on its own. The lock was not forced. That is the part that has taken the colour out of their face.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Find it before Thursday.
Make a replacement nobody will question.
Tell them to announce it from the altar.

fnd2.text:
It has not left {the building|the sacristy|the parish}. It is in a drawer in a room that is used by one person, wrapped in a cloth, with a note that is halfway to being a confession and does not get finished.
It goes back on the velvet before Thursday. Nobody is named. The party is asked for nothing and given {a great deal|more than they came with|everything the parish can spare}.

nof2.text:
Thursday comes and the reliquary is carried round the square at the correct pace by {six|eight} men who do not know what they are carrying.
It is a good feast. Everybody says so. The sacristan does not {eat|eat a thing|touch anything}.

fake.text:
It takes an evening and {qty} {material} and a great deal of care about the colour, and on the velvet under glass at three paces it is beyond question.
The procession goes round the square and the town gets its Thursday. What the party is left holding is the knowledge, which is heavier than the relic was.

tell.text:
It is announced from the altar on the Sunday, plainly, without an excuse attached, and the square goes very quiet and then does not fall apart.
By Thursday somebody has left it in the porch overnight in {a shoebox|a biscuit tin|a bag with a shop's name on it}, which is how these things have {always actually been resolved|generally been resolved|been settled since anybody can remember}.

qe_fence.title: {The Back Room|No Questions On Either Side|What Is In The Crate}

n0.text:
{fence} works out of a back room off {street} and has a crate that came in {timeAgo} that nobody has come to collect.
The arrangement on offer is the usual: the party moves it as far as {distance} and asks nothing, and is paid in {payment}. The crate is heavier at one end.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Take the job and do not open it.
Open it first.
Buy it outright and it is nobody's business but the party's.

job.text:
{distance}, delivered, signed for by somebody who does not give a name and does not need to.
The money is good and the walk back is the first time all week nobody has had to think about anything, and neither of those facts survives contact with what is in {rumour} a fortnight later.

opn.text:
Opened and re-nailed so that nobody could tell, which is a skill, and what is in it is worse than the money and better than the party feared.
Knowing changes the price. {fence} pays the new price without arguing, which says everything about what {fence} already knew.

opf.text:
The lid splinters at the corner and there is no putting that right with the tools to hand.
{fence} looks at the corner for a long moment and then says the job is off and the party should go, in a voice that has {nothing behind it at all|nothing in it|no weather in it whatsoever}.

own.text:
Bought, carried out through the front {for once|in daylight|without anybody ducking}, and opened on the party's own ground in the party's own time with nobody standing over it.
What is inside was worth considerably more than the asking price, which is what happens when a thing is priced by how badly somebody {wants it gone|needs it out of the room|wants rid}.

qe_dig.title: {The Contractor's Deadline|Bones Under The Foundation|Pour It Monday}

n0.text:
A site at {place} with the foundation dug and the pour booked for Monday, and something in the trench that stopped the machine on Friday.
{stranger} is the one who has to decide, and has been standing at the edge of the trench since. There is a carving on what is down there and it is older than the town.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Work it out properly. Two days, unpaid.
Shore it and pour around it, {qty} {material}.
Nothing was ever found here.

arch.text:
Two days on hands and knees and it is a boundary stone, in place, still doing its job, marking a line that every wall in {place} has quietly respected for eight hundred years without anybody knowing why.
That is a paper, and the paper has the party's names on it, and the Foundation pays for {papers|papers like that|a paper}.

archf.text:
Two days, and at the end of it the honest answer is that nobody in this trench is qualified to say what it is.
Monday arrives regardless. The pour happens. Whatever it was is under {a hundred|ninety|a hundred and twenty} cubic metres of concrete and will be somebody's problem in {the next century|a hundred years|whichever century digs it up}.

shore.text:
Shuttering, a void former, and the {material} to hold it: the pour goes ahead on Monday and the thing in the trench keeps a room to itself under the new floor.
It costs the contractor a weekend and it costs nobody the deadline, and there is a hatch, and the hatch is on {the drawings|the drawings, in ink|every set of the drawings}.

pour.text:
The machine goes back in on the Saturday and by Sunday night there is nothing in that trench but trench.
The pour goes ahead. {stranger} pays cash and does not shake anybody's hand, and the building goes up straight and stays up, which is not {the point|the point at all|what anybody was asking}.

qe_race.title: {Saturday On The Long Straight|Under Eighty Or Not At All|The Bet}

n0.text:
There is a straight outside {place} where they run on a Saturday, and the whole game is that the ones who win are the ones who do not go over.
Everybody knows where the bubble sits. {stranger} takes the money on the gate. {many} people are here for it and about half of them have opinions about {vehicle} the party arrived in.

asides.hedonistic: {member} has put money on somebody they have never met on the strength of a jacket.
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Put money on it.
Run it.
Flag the edge for them before somebody else goes over.

won2.text:
The one in the jacket holds it at {seventy-nine|seventy-eight|a shade under} the whole way down and takes it by a length and a half without ever once being interesting to look at, which is the entire art.
The gate pays out in cash and the party is bought drinks by strangers for {the rest of the evening|the rest of the night|hours}.

lost3.text:
The one in the jacket goes over at the {three-quarter mark|last marker|top of the straight}, which everybody in the crowd sees coming about a second before it happens.
The stake is gone and the jacket is gone, and the gate keeps taking money, because there is another one in {twenty minutes|half an hour|a quarter of an hour}.

ran.text:
Holding a thing at seventy-nine the whole length of the straight with a crowd screaming at you to do the one thing that will end you is not a driving problem, it is a nerve problem.
{leader} takes it at a walking pace by comparison to everybody else and wins, and the straight gives them the sort of silence that turns into a roar.

ranf.text:
It gets away at the top end for a moment and the moment is enough to be pulled at, and the pull is felt in the chest and the teeth before the brakes answer.
The party comes off the straight at a crawl with everybody very white. The crowd {applauds anyway|cheers anyway|makes a noise about it anyway}, which is {somehow worse|worse|the worst part of it}.

flag.text:
Posts and tape at the real edge, laid out in the afternoon before the crowd arrives, with the {material} the party carried in.
Saturday goes off with nobody lost for the first time in a season. The gate is furious for about an hour and then buys the party a drink, {twice|twice over|and then another}.

qe_orchard.title: {The Orchard Nobody Owns|A Season Of It|Windfalls}

n0.text:
There is an orchard behind {place} that has been unowned since {timeAgo}, and this year it has come in heavy enough to break its own branches.
{stranger} has been picking it alone for a week. Nobody else has come. The whole crop goes over in about four days if it is not taken.

asides.nurturing: {member} is up a ladder within about ninety seconds.
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Pick it. All of it.
Give {qty} {material} for crates and get the town up here.
Prune it properly for next year instead.

pick.text:
{Four|Five|Three} days of ladders and aching hands and more fruit than anybody has containers for, and it is all in before the weather turns.
The party leaves with as much as they can carry and the standing right to come back next year, which in a place like this is {a document|as good as a deed|worth more than paper}.

pickf.text:
The weather comes in on the second day and the rest goes over on the branch in a night.
What was got is worth having. What is left drops into the grass and feeds {animal} instead, which somebody older points out is {not nothing|not a waste|the older arrangement}.

town.text:
Crates, a cart, and word put about, and by the second morning there are {many} people in an orchard that nobody owns taking what they need and stacking the rest.
It goes to the school, the two houses on the corner, and a woman on {street} who has not asked anybody for anything in {timeAgo}.

prune.text:
The crop goes over and everybody agrees, out loud, that it was going to.
What gets done instead is the saw work nobody has done since {timeAgo}, and in {three|four} years that orchard will carry twice this and not break itself doing it, and none of that is visible {today|from here|this afternoon}.

n0.text:
{stranger} in {place} has a summons with somebody else's crime on it and their own name, spelled correctly, in a hand that never makes mistakes.
Her court does not do appeals in the usual sense. It does arbitrary, and it does it fast, and the hour named on the paper is tomorrow's.
